title: Tenant policy DSL + simulator for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We regularly tune prefill/decode arbitration to trade latency vs throughput while keeping multi-tenant fairness. Current heuristics live in C++ scheduler code and are hard to reason about per-tenant constraints (weights, latency SLOs, kernel affinity hints). That makes staged experiments slow and dangerous for Dedicated/Private customers that need predictable behaviour.

Goal:
Provide a small, composable policy DSL that operators and platform code can use to express tenant-level intent (e.g., soft latency SLO + best-effort throughput, kernel affinity for sparse-attention-friendly models, gradual degradation rules). Ship a simulator that consumes real arrival traces and kernel-cost estimates to evaluate policies before rollout.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Policy DSL grammar (JSON/YAML) supporting: weights, soft/hard SLOs, phase split hints, kernel affinity tags, hedging/backpressure rules, emergency demotion thresholds.
- Deterministic simulator that replays production prefill/decode traces (sampled from dev cluster) and outputs latency/throughput/fairness traces and per-tenant kernel selection counts.
- Integration shim in scheduler to accept policy bundles and a safe canary path (low-risk flag to enable on a percentage of machines).
- Dashboard notebook + benchmark harness for policy comparison (Jain's fairness, p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost proxy).

Design decisions so far:
- Use a declarative DSL rather than full sandboxed code: easier to validate and to expose to SREs/PMs.
- Policies are evaluated at admission and produce a composite vector: {priority_score, kernel_hint, phase_budget}. The scheduler uses these as tie-breakers; does not allow arbitrary code execution in hot path.
- Soft SLO semantics: allow bounded overrun with exponentially decaying credit to avoid oscillation during bursts.
- Kernel hints are advisory (strings: "sparse-friendly", "dense-fast", "quantized-v1"); runtime still considers capacity and may remap.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- DSL expressiveness vs runtime complexity: we intentionally avoid Turing-complete expressions; may require future extension points for custom fairness functions.
- Simulator fidelity: currently uses model-level kernel-cost profiles from profiler snapshots. We need to validate against real kernel latency traces (next sprint).
- Telemetry volume vs usefulness: per-tenant kernel selection counters are useful but increase cardinality; will roll up by kernel-tag in initial release.

Progress / experiments:
- Simulator prototype implemented (python) and validated on a 72-hour sampled trace from staging: baseline scheduler vs two policies (soft-latency-priority, throughput-economy). Results: soft-latency reduced p95 by ~28% for priority tenants with 9% throughput loss cluster-wide and Jain index improved for top-10 tenants.
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/TP-328/Policy+DSL+for+Prefill+-+Simulator (internal).
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 (simulator + DSL parser).

Acceptance criteria / rollout plan:
1) Simulator validated against gold traces and agrees within 10% on p95 and throughput metrics when compared to quick cluster canary.
2) Scheduler accepts policy bundle and exposes metrics for kernel hint remapping counts.
3) Canary: enable policy-based admission on 5% of capacity with automatic rollback on safety triggers (p95 increase > 20% for non-priority tenants).
4) Docs and runbook (how to author policies, how to interpret simulator reports).

Next steps (short term):
- Wire simulator to kernel-level telemetry (ENG-51399) to calibrate cost model (owner: Marco).
- Iterate DSL validation rules with SRE/Platform (owner: Aisha).
- Implement safe canary gating and automatic rollback hooks (owner: Marco).

Notes / follow-ups:
- We should discuss exposing a managed UI for basic policy templates (PM request) after stable canary.
- Consider extending DSL with "grace windows" for scheduled maintenance (future).
